title: Week of 13 November 2026
notes: New: the story of Prophet Ishaq, alayhis salaam (the next Prophet in order without a story), 21 gems on guests, sharing food, thankfulness, family duas and Allah's signs, and 10 Jumu'ah quiz questions. Sources: the Qur'an (Arabic copied word for word from the Tanzil simple text, the same spelling the app uses; meanings checked against the Saheeh International translation) and Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim (every hadith number checked on sunnah.com or hadithunlocked.com). abdurrahman.org could not be reached from this run, so the story relies on the Qur'an and the two Sahihs only. Please read carefully: the Qur'an tells very little about Ishaq's own life, so most of the story is the good news of his birth (Surah Hud, al-Hijr, adh-Dhariyat). It overlaps a little with Ibrahim part 2, but uses mostly different ayat. Slide 2 says Allah first gave Isma'il after Ibrahim's dua in as-Saffat 37:100, following the order of 37:101 and 37:112. Slide 5 says Ibrahim's wife laughed (fa-dahikat); some translations say smiled. Her name, Sarah, is left out because the Qur'an does not name her. Gem 17 (salawat) cites only Sahih al-Bukhari 3370 and gem 15 only al-Bukhari 3382, because a Muslim number could not be confirmed. Gem 11 is Sahih Muslim 2963 (sunnah.com lists it as 2963c).

stories.title: Prophet Ishaq, the promised son
stories.sub: Nothing is too hard for Allah, so never stop making dua

sc.label: A desert path between palm trees at sunrise

slides.text: Prophet Ibrahim, alayhis salaam, told his people to stop worshipping idols. When they would not listen, he left them for the sake of Allah. He said:

ay.ar: وَأَعْتَزِلُكُمْ وَمَا تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَأَدْعُو رَبِّي
ay.en: I will leave you and what you call on besides Allah, and I will call on my Rabb.

sc.label: A quiet night sky with one bright star

slides.text: Ibrahim was growing old, and he made dua to Allah for a good child. Allah gave him a son, Isma'il, alayhis salaam. And Allah had another gift waiting for him.

ay.en: My Rabb, give me a child who is one of the righteous.

sc.label: A small town at dusk with warm lit windows

slides.text: One day, guests came to Ibrahim's home and greeted him with salam. They were really angels sent by Allah, but Ibrahim did not know that yet.

ay.ar: هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الْمُكْرَمِينَ
ay.en: Has the story of Ibrahim's honoured guests reached you?

sc.label: A soft glow of light between palm trees in the evening

slides.text: Ibrahim hurried and brought them a fat roasted calf, the best food he had. But the guests did not eat, and Ibrahim felt afraid. They said:

ay.ar: قَالُوا لَا تَوْجَلْ إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَامٍ عَلِيمٍ
ay.en: Do not be afraid. We bring you good news of a boy who will have much knowledge.

sc.label: A green garden with flowers in the morning sun

slides.text: Ibrahim's wife was standing nearby, and she laughed. Then the angels gave her good news of a son called Ishaq, and after Ishaq, a grandson called Ya'qub.

ay.ar: فَبَشَّرْنَاهَا بِإِسْحَاقَ وَمِنْ وَرَاءِ إِسْحَاقَ يَعْقُوبَ
ay.en: So We gave her good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub.

sc.label: A white cloud over warm sand hills

slides.text: She was amazed, because she and Ibrahim were both very old. She said:

ay.ar: أَأَلِدُ وَأَنَا عَجُوزٌ وَهَٰذَا بَعْلِي شَيْخًا
ay.en: Will I have a baby when I am an old woman, and my husband here is an old man?

sc.label: A night sky full of stars over the desert

slides.text: The angels told them this was a promise from Allah, and nothing is too hard for Him. They said:

ay.ar: قَالُوا كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْعَلِيمُ
ay.en: That is what your Rabb has said. He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.

sc.label: Flowers and palm trees in the golden sunrise

slides.text: Allah's promise came true. Baby Ishaq, alayhis salaam, was born! Ibrahim thanked Allah and said:

ay.ar: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي وَهَبَ لِي عَلَى الْكِبَرِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ إِنَّ رَبِّي لَسَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ
ay.en: All praise is for Allah, who gave me Isma'il and Ishaq even though I am old. My Rabb truly hears every dua.

sc.label: An open book with a soft light beside it

slides.text: Ishaq grew up to be a Prophet and one of the righteous. Allah blessed Ibrahim and Ishaq (Surah as-Saffat 37:113).

ay.en: And We gave him good news of Ishaq, a Prophet, one of the righteous.

sc.label: A small town at night with lit windows under a crescent moon

slides.text: Allah made Ishaq and his son Ya'qub leaders who guided people. Allah told them to do good deeds, pray salah and give zakah, and they worshipped Allah alone.

ay.en: And We made them leaders, guiding by Our command.

sc.label: A lantern glowing beside an open book at night

slides.text: What do we learn? Never give up making dua, because nothing is too hard for Allah. Be generous to guests, like Ibrahim. And when Allah gives you something good, say Alhamdulillah, just like Ibrahim did.

quiz.q: Who brought Ibrahim the good news of Ishaq?
quiz.why: Angels came as guests and gave the good news (Surah adh-Dhariyat 51:24-28).

quiz.q: What food did Ibrahim bring for his guests?
quiz.why: Ibrahim was generous and brought a roasted calf (Surah Hud 11:69, Surah adh-Dhariyat 51:26).

quiz.q: Why was Ibrahim's wife amazed by the good news?
o: She and Ibrahim were very old
quiz.why: She said: Will I have a baby when I am an old woman and my husband is an old man? (Surah Hud 11:72)

quiz.q: What did Ibrahim say when Allah gave him Isma'il and Ishaq?
o: I did it all by myself
quiz.why: He said Alhamdulillah, all praise is for Allah, who gave me Isma'il and Ishaq (Surah Ibrahim 14:39).

gems.text: Prophet Zakariyya, alayhis salaam, made this dua: My Rabb, give me good children from You. You hear every dua.
gems.ar: رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ

gems.text: A family dua from the Qur'an: Our Rabb, make our families and children a joy for our eyes.
gems.ar: رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ

gems.text: When Allah wants something to happen, He only says to it: Be! And it is.
Allah gave Luqman wisdom and told him: Be thankful to Allah. Whoever is thankful, it is good for himself.
We believe in Allah and in what He sent to Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub, Musa, 'Isa and all the Prophets. We make no difference between any of them.
Allah gives daughters to whom He wants, and sons to whom He wants. Every child is a gift from Allah.
gems.ar: يَهَبُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ إِنَاثًا وَيَهَبُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ الذُّكُورَ

gems.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should be generous to his guest.
The Prophet ﷺ said: Food for two people is enough for three, and food for three is enough for four. So share your food!
Someone asked which deeds in Islam are best. The Prophet ﷺ said: Feed people, and say salam to those you know and those you do not know.
Allah is pleased with a person who eats a bite of food and says Alhamdulillah, and drinks and says Alhamdulillah.
Look at people who have less than you, not at those who have more. Then you will not forget how much Allah has given you.
The Prophet ﷺ said: The names Allah loves most are Abdullah and Abdur-Rahman.
When a person dies, his deeds stop, except three: charity that keeps helping, knowledge that helps people, and a good child who makes dua for him.
Allah gave Ibrahim his son Ishaq and his grandson Ya'qub, and He guided each one of them.
The Prophet ﷺ said: The noble one, son of the noble one, son of the noble one, son of the noble one: Yusuf, son of Ya'qub, son of Ishaq, son of Ibrahim.
Allah praised Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub: they were strong in obeying Allah, they saw the truth clearly, and they always remembered the Akhirah.
When we send salawat in our salah, we ask Allah to bless Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his family, just as He blessed Ibrahim and his family.
Allah lets two seas meet, but there is a barrier between them, so neither one takes over the other.
Grapes, crops and palm trees drink the very same water, yet Allah makes some fruits taste better than others.
Allah gives us pure, tasty milk to drink from inside grazing animals like cows, goats and camels.
People all over the world speak different languages and have different colours. This is one of Allah's signs!

quiz.q: Which Prophet was the son of Ibrahim and the father of Ya'qub?
quiz.why: Allah gave Ibrahim the good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub (Surah Hud 11:71).

quiz.q: What did the angels say when Ibrahim felt afraid?
o: Do not be afraid, we bring you good news
quiz.why: They said: Do not be afraid. We bring you good news of a boy (Surah al-Hijr 15:53).

quiz.q: Whose promise was the good news of Ishaq?
quiz.why: The angels said: That is what your Rabb has said (Surah adh-Dhariyat 51:30).

quiz.q: What did Allah make Ishaq when he grew up?
o: A Prophet and one of the righteous
A king of a big city
quiz.why: We gave him good news of Ishaq, a Prophet, one of the righteous (Surah as-Saffat 37:112).

quiz.q: What does Allah say when He wants something to happen?
quiz.why: He only says to it: Be! And it is (Surah Ya-Sin 36:82).

quiz.q: Food for two people is enough for how many?
quiz.why: The Prophet ﷺ said food for two is enough for three (Sahih al-Bukhari 5392, Sahih Muslim 2058).

quiz.q: What should we say after we eat or drink?
quiz.why: Allah is pleased with the one who praises Him after eating and drinking (Sahih Muslim 2734).

quiz.q: Which names does Allah love most?
quiz.why: The Prophet ﷺ said so (Sahih Muslim 2132).

quiz.q: To remember Allah's blessings, who should we look at?
o: People who have less than us
People who have more than us
quiz.why: Then we will not forget how much Allah has given us (Sahih Muslim 2963).

quiz.q: Who was the grandson of Prophet Ishaq?
quiz.why: Yusuf, son of Ya'qub, son of Ishaq, son of Ibrahim (Sahih al-Bukhari 3382).
